Is the intended answer that "courses" means the dishes of a banquet menu, so that choosing courses before the deadline meant choosing the menu, and on the night all the courses were served and cleared away, leaving none?

The wordplay is on "courses." You are not picking academic classes; you are a guest at a formal University of Hong Kong hall/society banquet, and you "chose your courses" by submitting your menu selections before the menu deadline. The evening of the banquet then arrived.

On the night, the dinner was served course by course by the catering staff. Every dish you had chosen was brought out — the Chinese banquet custom where each course is presented and then the plates are cleared away. As the meal progressed, dish after dish was carried off to be shared out and cleared once served. You ate at least one of the courses, but you also waved away some of the dishes, so not everything passed through your own plate.

Because the banquet ran through the evening as a sequence of courses — each served and then removed — by the end of that single evening every one of the "courses" you had selected was gone: all had been served and cleared away. The source of the confusion is that "choosing courses before the deadline" ordinarily sounds like course registration at university, but here it referred to selecting the dishes for a banquet, and those courses "disappeared in one evening" simply because they were served and taken away over the course of the dinner.

The trick is the double meaning of "courses." You are not registering for academic classes at all — you are a student who is a guest at a formal hall/society banquet, and "choosing your courses before the deadline" meant submitting your menu selections (the dishes) for the dinner before the menu deadline.

On the evening of the banquet, the catering staff served the meal course by course. Every dish you had chosen was brought out and, in the usual banquet style, each course was presented to the table and then the plates were cleared away once it had been served. You did eat at least one of the courses yourself, but there were also some courses you declined or waved away rather than taking a portion.

So what happened is that the "courses" you had chosen did not vanish from any enrollment system: over that one evening they were all served one after another and then removed and cleared away. By the end of the night, every course was "gone" because the banquet had progressed through the whole menu and the staff had taken each dish away — the entire meal had come and gone in a single evening. The confusion comes from reading "courses" and "deadline" as university course registration, when in fact they referred to choosing dishes for a banquet.
